title: Sattu Paratha
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion and ginger.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, ajwain, mustard oil, lemon, salt

recipe: Mix sattu with chopped onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, ajwain, mustard oil, lemon juice and salt to make the filling.
Knead a soft wheat dough. Stuff portions with the sattu mixture, seal and roll into parathas.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee till golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or chutney.
tips: Classic Bihari breakfast – protein-rich and cooling due to sattu.
Mustard oil in the filling is essential for authentic flavour.

title: Chura Dahi (Dahi Chura)
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (flattened rice, curd, jaggery, fruit). Ensure curd is made without gelatin.

ingredients.name: Jaggery or sugar, banana or mango (seasonal)

recipe: Wash and lightly soak the chura if needed. Drain.
Mix with thick curd and jaggery or sugar. Add sliced banana or mango in season.
Serve as a light, cooling breakfast – especially popular in summer and on Makar Sankranti.
tips: Simple, probiotic Bihari breakfast – Katarni chura is prized when available.
Refreshing and easy to digest.

title: Puri with Aloo Sabzi
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger, spices
Oil for deep frying, ghee or oil for sabzi

recipe: Knead a stiff dough for puris. Roll and deep-fry till puffed and golden.
Prepare a simple spiced potato sabzi with onion, tomato and ginger.
Serve hot puris with the sabzi, often accompanied by jalebi or a sweet on special days.
tips: Classic festive or Sunday breakfast across Bihar.
Puris should be light and well-puffed.

title: Litti Chokha
jainNotes: Contains onion, garlic, ginger - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Sattu, mustard oil, garlic, ginger, green chilli, ajwain, lemon, salt
Onion, mustard oil, green chilli for chokha

recipe: Prepare sattu stuffing with mustard oil, garlic, ginger, chilli, ajwain, lemon and salt. Stuff into wheat dough balls and seal.
Roast the littis over charcoal, cow-dung cakes, or bake till the crust is crisp and slightly charred.
For chokha: Roast brinjal, tomato and boil potato. Mash with onion, green chilli, mustard oil and salt.
Dip hot littis in ghee and serve with chokha.
tips: The iconic dish of Bihar – smoky, rustic and deeply satisfying.
Traditional open-fire roasting gives the authentic flavour.

title: Dal Bhaat with Chana Dal & Sabzi
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger-garlic, spices
Seasonal vegetable sabzi, chokha, papad, pickle, curd

recipe: Cook rice and a simple tempered chana dal with onion, tomato and spices.
Prepare a dry or gravy vegetable sabzi and a side of chokha.
Serve the classic Bihari thali of rice, dal, sabzi, chokha, papad, pickle and curd.
tips: Everyday Bihari lunch – simple, balanced and comforting.
Curd is almost always present on the plate.

title: Dal Bhaat with Mixed Dal & Sabzi
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger-garlic, spices
Seasonal vegetable sabzi, chokha, papad, pickle, curd

recipe: Cook rice and a simple tempered mixed dal with onion, tomato and spices.
Prepare a dry or gravy vegetable sabzi and a side of chokha.
Serve the classic Bihari thali of rice, dal, sabzi, chokha, papad, pickle and curd.
tips: Everyday Bihari lunch made with mixed lentils.
Simple, balanced and nourishing.

title: Kadhi Bari
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.
recipe: Make soft besan dumplings (bari), deep-fry and set aside.
Prepare a yogurt-besan kadhi, tempered with spices and ginger. Add the fried bari and simmer.
Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Comforting Bihari kadhi with soft fried dumplings.
A popular home-style dish.

title: Bihari Mutton Curry
jainNotes: Contains mutton, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Garam masala, red chilli, turmeric, oil

recipe: Marinate mutton with yogurt and spices. Sauté onion and ginger-garlic till golden.
Add the mutton and cook till tender in a rich, spiced gravy.
Serve with roti, litti or rice – often a celebratory dish.
tips: Non-vegetarian food is typically reserved for special occasions in many Bihari homes.
Slow cooking yields the best results.

title: Bihari Fish Curry
jainNotes: Contains fish, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Lightly fry fish pieces in mustard oil. Prepare a gravy with onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and spices.
Add the fish and simmer gently.
Serve with rice.
tips: Common in riverine and Mithila regions of Bihar.
Mustard oil is the preferred cooking medium.

title: Bihari Fish Curry with Mustard (Angika Style)
jainNotes: Contains fish, onion, garlic, mustard - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, onion, tomato, ginger-garlic, mustard paste

recipe: Lightly fry fish pieces in mustard oil. Prepare a gravy with onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and spices.
Add mustard paste and the fish. Simmer gently.
Serve with rice.
tips: Angika-style fish curry with mustard paste for extra pungency.
Common in the Mithila and Angika regions of Bihar.

title: Thekua
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (wheat flour, jaggery, ghee, cardamom). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.

ingredients.name: Oil or ghee for deep frying

recipe: Melt jaggery with a little water. Mix into wheat flour with ghee and cardamom to form a stiff dough.
Shape into small discs or use traditional moulds. Deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp.
Cool and store. Especially made for Chhath Puja.
tips: Iconic Chhath festival sweet of Bihar – crisp, mildly sweet and long-lasting.
Ghee in the dough improves flavour and texture.

title: Ghugni with White Peas
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion and ginger.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger, green chilli, spices
Mustard oil, lemon, coriander for garnish

recipe: Pressure-cook the soaked white peas till soft. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with mustard oil.
Add the peas and simmer. Garnish with onion, green chilli, coriander and lemon.
Serve hot as a snack or with muri (puffed rice).
tips: Popular street and home snack made with white peas.
Often eaten with puffed rice (ghugni-muri) in the Anga region.

title: Ghugni with Black Chickpeas
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion and ginger.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger, green chilli, spices
Mustard oil, lemon, coriander for garnish

recipe: Pressure-cook the soaked black chickpeas till soft. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with mustard oil.
Add the chickpeas and simmer. Garnish with onion, green chilli, coriander and lemon.
Serve hot as a snack or with muri (puffed rice).
tips: Popular street and home snack made with black chickpeas.
Often eaten with puffed rice (ghugni-muri) in the Anga region.

title: Dal Pitha
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.
recipe: Cook and grind spiced chana dal into a filling. Make a soft rice-flour dough.
Stuff portions of dough with the dal mixture, shape into parcels and steam or boil till cooked.
Serve with chutney or a light tempering.
tips: Steamed rice-flour dumplings with spiced dal filling – light and nourishing.
A traditional Bihari comfort dish.

title: Aloo Chokha
jainNotes: Contains onion and potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Onion, green chilli, mustard oil, salt

recipe: Mash the boiled potatoes while warm. Mix with finely chopped onion, green chilli, raw mustard oil and salt.
Serve with litti, roti or as a side.
tips: Simple, pungent mashed potato preparation – a staple side in Bihari meals.
Raw mustard oil is the key flavouring.
